To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
androstenedion induces cell proliferation and decrease apoptosis in the stromals cells of the endometrial explants and in the stromal cells in culture.

androstenediol increases the cell proliferation and decreases the apoptosis in the stroma and increases the ER-beta mRNA expression in the epithelial cells, without an effect on the apoptotic index in the endometrial cells.
androstenedion may modulate cell proliferation, apoptosis and expression of proteins related to apoptosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of endometrial cells and the effect of androgens and their potential role on cell proliferation and apoptosis.
the effect of androgens in the endometrium and their role in the pathophysiology of the endometrium.
the effect of androgens in endometrial cell proliferation, cell survival and expression of ER and proteins related to cell death.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effect of androgens in endometrial cell proliferation and apoptosis depends on cell types, and that the effect on apoptosis is not a direct effect of androstene.

the results obtained in this study are in accordance with the hypothesis that androgens, through their action on stromal endometrium cells, may be involved in endometrial pathogenesis, especially when hyperandrogenemia is present.

the effect of hyper-androgenism on cell survival, apoptosis, ER expression, and proteins related to the apoptotic pathway, may be mediated by androgens and androgen receptors in the endometrial stromal cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
androstenedine has a proliferative and apoptotic effect on endometrial cells and that these actions could be mediated by the modulation of estrogen receptors and bax/bcl-2 ratio.
androstenedion can modulate cell proliferation and cell death in endometrial tissue, through the expression of ER-beta isoform and the bcl- 2/bax ratio.

androstenedion may modulate cell proliferation, apoptosis, and ER-beta and proteins associated with apoptosis, suggesting that androgens may be a potential factor for the endometrial pathogenesis in women with hyperandrogenemia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
androgens can have an impact on cell survival in endometrial tissue, which could be related with the pathophysiology of endometrial diseases.
the effect of androgens is different between the two cell types, and that the effect is mediated by androgen receptor.
androgen receptors in endometrial stromal cells may have a role in the regulation of proliferation and apoptosis.
